title: Find affix pairs in words
description: Reads a plain word list (a TSV of form and count, or a folder of text files) with no project and finds pairs of words that differ only by a suffix or prefix, with the bases, tokens and examples of each differing part and the parts each base takes. Optional regular expression on the differing part, bases having all of several parts, bounded and deterministic.
helpPage:
# Query pairs

`motif query pairs --corpus <words.tsv|folder> --differ suffix|prefix` (or `motif query --corpus <words.tsv|folder> pairs --differ suffix|prefix`) finds pairs of words of a plain word list that differ only by an affix: a base and base+X (suffix) or X+base (prefix). It needs no project, Trial or parse, and changes nothing.

```powershell
motif query --corpus words.tsv pairs --differ suffix
motif query --corpus texts/ pairs --differ suffix --x 'an|in' --having an,in --json
```

## The corpus

A TSV has one word per line, `form<TAB>count<TAB>parse state`. The header is optional; a first line starting `form` or `word` names the columns (`count`, `tokens` or `frequency`; `state` or `parse.state`). A missing count is 1. A folder is every `.txt` file in it, tokenised on Unicode letters and combining marks; an apostrophe (U+0027, U+2019, U+02BC) or hyphen-minus between letters stays inside the word (`ng'ombe`), and `--split-hyphens` splits at hyphens. Forms are NFC; `--fold-case` also lower-cases them, and folds `--having` and matches `--x` ignoring case. Segments are code points and the result says `approximate`. `--segments <file>` lists multi-character graphemes, such as `ng ny ch`, separated by spaces, tabs, commas or lines, with `#` comments; the longest match wins.

## The result

Per X: the bases that take it, the tokens of those derived forms, the tokens of the bases and the example pairs with the most tokens. Per base: the Xs it takes. `--x <regex>` keeps the Xs the whole differing part matches (non-backtracking). `--having a,b` keeps the bases that take all of the listed Xs. `--max-x` (1 to 12, default 4) caps the length of X in segments, `--limit` (default 100) caps the X rows and the base rows, and `--examples` (default 5) caps the examples. A cut is stated: `TRUNCATED: showing 100 of 412 Xs`, and in JSON the `truncation` object holds the totals and shown counts. Rows are in a fixed order, so a run is reproducible. `--json` writes `motif.query.pairs.v1`.
